chunks: And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said:
"Whoever leaves forbidding the evil with his heart, hand, and tongue, he is a dead person among the living."
At the end of this speech.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean to be 'dead among the living' in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In this profound statement from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines spiritual death not as the cessation of breath, but as the paralysis of the three faculties—heart, hand, and tongue—in executing *Amr bil Ma'ruf*. This narration underscores the Shia scholarly view that passive acceptance of evil constitutes a state of living death, emphasizing that true vitality lies in active moral vigilance. It serves as a critical reminder that the failure to utilize any of these three modes of forbidding evil results in a loss of spiritual essence while the body remains alive.
